metadata.case_name: HO SHUN HANG v. LAU HOI WING AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: tram driver (motorman) employed by the Hong Kong Tramways Limited
plaintiff.occupation_after: tram driver (resumed duties, light duties from July 2006)

source: Physical examination showed tenderness on his neck region with limitation in range of motion.
Radiological examination of his cervical spine showed loss of lordosis.
injuries.icd_description: Acute whiplash associated disorder with complaint of neck pain with musculoskeletal signs

source: The experts were of the view that the Plaintiff suffered from abrasion of the left hand and sprained injury of the neck.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified superficial injury of other parts of wrist or hand

source: He was diagnosed to have adjustment disorder with depressed mood and was referred to clinical psychologist for counseling and admitted to the Psychiatric Day Hospital on 30 November 2005.
I found the Plaintiff also suffered from adjustment disorder in the third stage.

manifestations.description: limitation in range of motion of neck
loss of lordosis of the cervical spine
referred symptom down to the wrist
insomnia / poor sleep (waking up at night)
anxiousness and lowish mood / depressed mood
auditory perception of sound ("sound of insect at both ears")
requires escort to get medicine, take a bath, and walk in the street

treatments_received.treatment: hospital admission and in-patient orthopaedic care (Eastern Hospital) - 6 April 2004 and 20-24 May 2004
source: after the accident, he was rushed to Ruttonjee and Tang Shiu Kin Hospital for treatment. He was later transferred to Pamela Youde Nethersole Eastern Hospital ("Eastern Hospital") and was admitted to the Department of Orthopedics and Traumatology.
The Plaintiff was discharged on 7 April 2004 and was then followed up in the outpatient clinic of Eastern Hospital.
The Plaintiff said he was re-admitted to the Eastern Hospital on 20 May 2005 because of exacerbation of neck pain. He was discharged on 24May 2005.

treatments_received.treatment: physiotherapy (Eastern Hospital) – courses from 3 May 2004 to 19 May 2004; 12 July 2004 to 13 August 2004; and from 2 August 2005 to 18 May 2006
source: The Plaintiff received physiotherapy treatment. He was then suffering from dizziness, neck pain with referred symptom down to the wrist. He stopped physiotherapy treatment after 13 August 2004.

The Plaintiff was referred for physiotherapy treatment for neck injury and attended another course of treatment from 2 August 2005 in Eastern Hospital. He was discharged from physiotherapy on 18 May 2006 with advice on home exercise.

treatments_received.treatment: psychiatric treatment / admission to Psychiatric Day Hospital and outpatient psychiatry follow-up (Eastern Hospital)
source: He was referred to the psychiatry unit of Eastern Hospital in October 2005. He was diagnosed to have adjustment disorder with depressed mood and was referred to clinical psychologist for counseling and admitted to the Psychiatric Day Hospital on 30 November 2005. He continued to attend the Psychiatric Day Hospital until April 2006.

The Plaintiff attended the emergency department of Eastern Hospital on 1 December 2008 and was referred to the psychiatric unit. He was hospitalized until 10 December 2008 and followed up at the psychiatric unit of Eastern Hospital.
He took analgesic medicine four times a day and every day.

treatments_received.treatment: sleeping pills / medications from private doctor after defaulting Eastern Hospital psychiatric treatment
source: the Plaintiff obtained painkillers, sleeping pills from private doctor after he defaulted treatment of Eastern Hospital, Department of Psychiatry.
He was diagnosed to have adjustment disorder with depressed mood and was referred to clinical psychologist for counseling and admitted to the Psychiatric Day Hospital on 30 November 2005.

losses.description: Persistent neck pain with limitation of range of motion and residual neck symptoms following sprain of the neck/cervical spine.
Adjustment disorder with depressed mood causing anxiousness, low mood, poor sleep and related psychiatric symptoms.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Plaintiff reported he did not want to go out as he felt that people were laughing at him.
Plaintiff required escort to get his medicine, take a bath, and walk in the street.
